entries.title: Isaiah 39:1
segments:
. 
 
  King of Babylon; Babylon was at this time a dependency of Assyria, and governed by viceroys.  But Merodach-baladan, as history informs us, sought to make himself independent.  For this reason, probably, he courted the friendship of Hezekiah. 
 
See

entries.title: Isaiah 39:2
segments: Was glad of them, and showed them; he was unduly elated in view of the attention shown him by the king of Babylon, as well as of his own power and riches.

entries.title: Isaiah 39:7
segments: Of thy sons--they shall be eunuchs; this was fulfilled, not in his immediate offspring, but in their posterity.  See
, where by "the king's seed" are meant the descendants of the Jewish kings.

entries.title: Isaiah 39:8
segments: For there shall be peace; he expresses his gratitude to God for this mitigation of the threatened chastisement.
